[JEE Main 2021, 25 July (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Shortest wavelength in a spectral series corresponds to transition from \( n = \infty \) to the series limit level.

- For Lyman series, lower level is \( n = 1 \)
\[
\frac{1}{\lambda_L} = R \left( \frac{1}{1^2} - \frac{1}{\infty^2} \right) = R
\Rightarrow \lambda_L = \frac{1}{R}
\]

- For Balmer series, lower level is \( n = 2 \)
\[
\frac{1}{\lambda_B} = R \left( \frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{\infty^2} \right) = R \cdot \frac{1}{4}
\Rightarrow \lambda_B = \frac{4}{R}
\]

Now, taking the ratio:

\[
\frac{\lambda_B}{\lambda_L} = \frac{4/R}{1/R} = 4 : 1
\]

questions.question:
The density of ' \(x\) ' M solution (' \(x\) ' molar) of NaOH is 1.12 g mL-1, while in molality, the concentration of the solution is 3 m (3 molal). Then \(x\) is
(Given : Molar mass of NaOH is 40 g/mol )
questions.explanation:
• Density of solution = 1.12 g/mL

  • Molality (m) = 3 mol/kg

  • Molar mass of NaOH = 40 g/mol

  • Molarity (x) = ?

We are to find the molarity xx (in mol/L) of NaOH.

Molality m=mol of solutemass of solvent in kgm = \frac{\text{mol of solute}}{\text{mass of solvent in kg}}

Given:

Molality=3 mol/kg\text{Molality} = 3 \, \mathrm{mol/kg}

Let’s assume we have 1 kg (1000 g) of water. Then the number of moles of NaOH = 3 mol.

Mass of NaOH =

3 mol×40 g/mol=120 g3 \, \text{mol} \times 40 \, \mathrm{g/mol} = 120 \, \mathrm{g}

So total mass of solution =

1000 g (water)+120 g (NaOH)=1120 g1000 \, \mathrm{g} \text{ (water)} + 120 \, \mathrm{g} \text{ (NaOH)} = 1120 \, \mathrm{g}

Given density = 1.12 g/mL 

So for 1120 g of solution:

Volume=1120 g1.12 g/mL=1000 mL=1 L\text{Volume} = \frac{1120 \, \mathrm{g}}{1.12 \, \mathrm{g/mL}} = 1000 \, \mathrm{mL} = 1 \, \mathrm{L}

Molarity x=mol of solutevolume of solution in Lx = \frac{\text{mol of solute}}{\text{volume of solution in L}}

We have 3.0 mol NaOH in 1 L of solution

x = 3.0

questions.question:
The function fx=x2+2x-15x2-4x+9,x∈R is 

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The function is

\(f(x)=\dfrac{x^2+2x-15}{x^2-4x+9}\).

The denominator is

\(x^2-4x+9=(x-2)^2+5>0\)

for every \(x\in\mathbb R\).

Therefore, the domain of \(f\) is \(\mathbb R\).

Let

\(y=\dfrac{x^2+2x-15}{x^2-4x+9}\).

Then

\(y(x^2-4x+9)=x^2+2x-15\).

Rearranging,

\((y-1)x^2-(4y+2)x+(9y+15)=0\).

For a real value of \(x\), the discriminant of this quadratic equation must be non-negative.

Therefore,

\((4y+2)^2-4(y-1)(9y+15)\geq0\).

On simplifying,

\(-4(5y^2+2y-16)\geq0\).

Hence,

\(5y^2+2y-16\leq0\).

Now,

\(5y^2+2y-16=(5y-8)(y+2)\).

Therefore,

\(-2\leq y\leq\dfrac85\).

Thus, the range of \(f\) is not \(\mathbb R\), so \(f\) is not onto.

Also,

\(f(0)=-\dfrac53\).

Further,

\(f\left(\dfrac74\right)=\dfrac{\frac{49}{16}+\frac72-15}{\frac{49}{16}-7+9}=-\dfrac53\).

Since

\(0\ne\dfrac74\)

but

\(f(0)=f\left(\dfrac74\right)\),

the function is not one-one.

Therefore, \(f\) is neither one-one nor onto.

questions.question:
Let f:(-∞,∞)-{0}→ℝ be a differentiable function such that \(f^{\prime}(1)=\lim _{a \rightarrow \infty} a^2 f\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)\). Then lima→∞a(a+1)2tan-11a+a2-2logea is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(x=\dfrac1a\).

Then \(a=\dfrac1x\) and \(\log_e a=-\log_e x\).

We need

\(a^2f\left(\dfrac1a\right)=\dfrac{a(a+1)}2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac1a\right)+a^2-2\log_e a\).

Replacing \(\dfrac1a\) by \(x\), this gives

\(\dfrac1{x^2}f(x)=\dfrac{1+x}{2x^2}\tan^{-1}x+\dfrac1{x^2}+2\log_e x\).

Multiplying by \(x^2\),

\(f(x)=\dfrac{1+x}{2}\tan^{-1}x+1+2x^2\log_e x\).

Now differentiate:

\(f'(x)=\dfrac12\tan^{-1}x+\dfrac{1+x}{2(1+x^2)}+4x\log_e x+2x\).

At \(x=1\), \(\tan^{-1}1=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) and \(\log_e1=0\).

Therefore,

\(f'(1)=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\dfrac{2}{2(2)}+0+2\).

Hence,

\(f'(1)=\dfrac{\pi}{8}+\dfrac12+2=\dfrac52+\dfrac{\pi}{8}\).

By the given condition,

\(\displaystyle\lim_{a\to\infty}a^2f\left(\dfrac1a\right)=f'(1)\)

Therefore, the intended value of the displayed limit is \(\dfrac52+\dfrac{\pi}{8}\)

questions.question:
The interval in which the function f(x)=xx,x>0, is strictly increasing is

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The function is \(f(x)=x^x\), where \(x>0\)

Taking the natural logarithm,

\(\log_e f(x)=x\log_e x\)

Differentiating both sides,

\(\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}=\log_e x+1\)

Therefore, \(f'(x)=f(x)(\log_e x+1)\)

Since \(f(x)=x^x>0\),

\(f'(x)=x^x(\log_e x+1)\)

The sign of \(f'(x)\) is determined by \(\log_e x+1\)

For the function to be increasing,

\(\log_e x+1\geq0\)

Therefore, \(\log_e x\geq-1\)

Since the exponential function is increasing,

\(x\geq e^{-1}=\dfrac1e\)

For \(0<x<\dfrac1e\),

\(\log_e x+1<0\)

so \(f'(x)<0\)

For \(x>\dfrac1e\)

\(\log_e x+1>0\),

so \(f'(x)>0\)

At \(x=\dfrac1e\),

\(f'(x)=0\)

Therefore, the function is strictly increasing on \(\left[\dfrac1e,\infty\right)\)

questions.question:
Let a variable line of slope m>0 passing through the point (4,-9)  intersect the coordinate axes at the points \(A\)  and \(B\). The minimum value of the sum of the distances of \(A\)  and \(B\)  from the origin is

\(y+9=m(x-4)\)

At the \(x\)-axis, \(y=0\),

so \(9=m(x-4)\)

Therefore, the \(x\)-intercept is \(4+\dfrac{9}{m}\)

and \(OA=4+\dfrac{9}{m}\)

At the \(y\)-axis, \(x=0\)

so \(y=-4m-9\)

Therefore, \(OB=|-4m-9|=4m+9\)

Hence \(OA+OB=13+4m+\dfrac{9}{m}\)

By the arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality,

\(4m+\dfrac{9}{m}\geq2\sqrt{4m\cdot\dfrac{9}{m}}=12\)

Equality occurs when \(4m=\dfrac{9}{m}\),

so \(m=\dfrac{3}{2}\)

Therefore, the minimum value is \(13+12=25\)

questions.question:
∫0π/4cos2xsin2xcos3x+sin3x2dx is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Given integral is \(I=\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{\cos^2x\sin^2x}{(\cos^3x+\sin^3x)^2}\,dx\)

Put \(\tan x=t\)

Then \(\sec^2x\,dx=dt\), so \(dx=\frac{dt}{1+t^2}\)

Also, \(\sin x=\frac{t}{\sqrt{1+t^2}}\) and \(\cos x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+t^2}}\)

So, \(\cos^2x\sin^2x=\frac{t^2}{(1+t^2)^2}\)

Now, \(\cos^3x+\sin^3x=\frac{1}{(1+t^2)^{3/2}}+\frac{t^3}{(1+t^2)^{3/2}}\)

Therefore, \(\cos^3x+\sin^3x=\frac{1+t^3}{(1+t^2)^{3/2}}\)

So, \((\cos^3x+\sin^3x)^2=\frac{(1+t^3)^2}{(1+t^2)^3}\)

When \(x=0\), \(t=0\), and when \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\), \(t=1\)

Therefore, \(I=\int_0^1 \frac{\frac{t^2}{(1+t^2)^2}}{\frac{(1+t^3)^2}{(1+t^2)^3}}\cdot\frac{dt}{1+t^2}\)

\(I=\int_0^1 \frac{t^2}{(1+t^3)^2}\,dt\)

Put \(1+t^3=u\)

Then \(3t^2\,dt=du\), so \(t^2\,dt=\frac{du}{3}\)

When \(t=0\), \(u=1\), and when \(t=1\), \(u=2\)

Therefore, \(I=\frac{1}{3}\int_1^2 \frac{du}{u^2}\)

\(I=\frac{1}{3}\left[-\frac{1}{u}\right]_1^2\)

\(I=\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{1}{2}+1\right)\)

\(I=\frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\)

\(I=\frac{1}{6}\)

Hence, the value of the integral is \(\frac{1}{6}\)

questions.question:
Let the area of the region enclosed by the curves y=3x,2y=27-3x  and y=3x-xx be \(A\). Then \(10 A\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The three curves are \(y=3x\), \(y=\dfrac{27-3x}{2}\), and \(y=3x-x\sqrt{x}\).

The two lines intersect when \(3x=\dfrac{27-3x}{2}\).

Thus \(6x=27-3x\), so \(9x=27\).

Therefore, the lines intersect at \(x=3\) and \(y=9\).

The curve \(y=3x-x\sqrt{x}\) meets \(y=3x\) when \(x\sqrt{x}=0\).

Since \(x\geq0\), this gives \(x=0\).

The curve meets \(y=\dfrac{27-3x}{2}\) when \(3x-x\sqrt{x}=\dfrac{27-3x}{2}\).

Multiplying by \(2\), we get \(6x-2x\sqrt{x}=27-3x\).

Thus \(9x-2x\sqrt{x}-27=0\).

Let \(t=\sqrt{x}\), so \(x=t^2\).

Then \(2t^3-9t^2+27=0\).

Factoring, \((t-3)^2(2t+3)=0\).

Since \(t\geq0\), we get \(t=3\), so \(x=9\) and \(y=0\).

For \(0\leq x\leq3\), the upper boundary is \(y=3x\).

For \(3\leq x\leq9\), the upper boundary is \(y=\dfrac{27-3x}{2}\).

The lower boundary is \(y=3x-x\sqrt{x}\).

Hence \(A=\displaystyle\int_0^3 x^{3/2}dx+\int_3^9\left(\dfrac{27-3x}{2}-3x+x^{3/2}\right)dx\).

Thus \(A=\displaystyle\int_0^3 x^{3/2}dx+\int_3^9\left(\dfrac{27}{2}-\dfrac{9x}{2}+x^{3/2}\right)dx\).

The first integral is \(\left[\dfrac{2x^{5/2}}{5}\right]_0^3=\dfrac{18\sqrt{3}}{5}\).

An antiderivative for the second integral is \(\dfrac{27x}{2}-\dfrac{9x^2}{4}+\dfrac{2x^{5/2}}{5}\).

At \(x=9\), its value is \(\dfrac{243}{2}-\dfrac{729}{4}+\dfrac{486}{5}=\dfrac{729}{20}\).

At \(x=3\), its value is \(\dfrac{81}{2}-\dfrac{81}{4}+\dfrac{18\sqrt{3}}{5}=\dfrac{81}{4}+\dfrac{18\sqrt{3}}{5}\).

Therefore, the second integral is \(\dfrac{729}{20}-\dfrac{81}{4}-\dfrac{18\sqrt{3}}{5}=\dfrac{81}{5}-\dfrac{18\sqrt{3}}{5}\).

Hence \(A=\dfrac{18\sqrt{3}}{5}+\dfrac{81}{5}-\dfrac{18\sqrt{3}}{5}=\dfrac{81}{5}\).

Therefore, \(10A=162\), which is option \(A\).

questions.question:
Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation 1+x2dydx+y=etan-1x, y(1)=0. Then y(0) is

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The differential equation is

\((1+x^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=e^{\tan^{-1}x}\)

Dividing by \(1+x^2\), we get

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}y=\dfrac{e^{\tan^{-1}x}}{1+x^2}\)

The integrating factor is

\(\mathrm{I.F.}=e^{\int\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx}=e^{\tan^{-1}x}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(ye^{\tan^{-1}x}\right)=\dfrac{e^{2\tan^{-1}x}}{1+x^2}\)

Put \(t=\tan^{-1}x\).

\(\Rightarrow dt=\dfrac{dx}{1+x^2}\)

\(\Rightarrow ye^t=\displaystyle\int e^{2t}\,dt=\dfrac{1}{2}e^{2t}+C\)

\(\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{1}{2}e^t+Ce^{-t}\)

Using \(y(1)=0\) and \(t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\), we get

\(0=\dfrac{1}{2}e^{\pi/4}+Ce^{-\pi/4}\)

\(\Rightarrow C=-\dfrac{1}{2}e^{\pi/2}\)

At \(x=0\), \(t=0\).

\(\Rightarrow y(0)=\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{2}e^{\pi/2}=\dfrac{1}{2}(1-e^{\pi/2})\)

The correct option is \(B\).

The differential equation is

Dividing by \(2x\ln x\), we get

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{1}{x\ln x}y=\dfrac{3}{2x^2}\)

The integrating factor is

\(\mathrm{I.F.}=e^{\int\frac{1}{x\ln x}\,dx}=\ln x\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{d}{dx}(y\ln x)=\dfrac{3\ln x}{2x^2}\)

Using integration by parts, we get

\(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\ln x}{x^2}\,dx=-\dfrac{\ln x+1}{x}\)

\(\Rightarrow y\ln x=-\dfrac{3(\ln x+1)}{2x}+C\)

Using \(y(e^{-1})=0\), we get

\(\Rightarrow C=0\)

At \(x=e\), we get

\(\Rightarrow y(e)=-\dfrac{3(1+1)}{2e}=-\dfrac{3}{e}\)

The correct option is \(C\).

Hence \(r_k-1=\dfrac{1}{k+1}\).

Thus, \(\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{10}\dfrac{1}{7(r_k-1)}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{10}\dfrac{k+1}{7}=\dfrac{1}{7}\left(\dfrac{10\cdot11}{2}+10\right)=\dfrac{65}{7}\).

questions.question: Let the first term of a series be T1=6 and its rth  term Tr=3Tr-1+6r,r=2,3,....... \(n\). If the sum of the first \(n\) terms of this series is 15n2-12n+394·6n-5·3n+1, then \(n\) is equal to _____

Let a conic \(C\) pass through the point \((4,-2)\) and P(x,y),x≥3, be any point on \(C\). Let the slope of the line touching the conic \(C\) only at a single point \(P\) be half the slope of the line joining the points \(P\) and (3,-5). If the focal distance of the point (7,1) on \(C\) is \(d\), then \(12 d\) equals  ____

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
At \(P(x,y)\), the tangent slope is half the slope of the line joining \(P\) to \((3,-5)\).

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{y+5}{x-3}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{2\,dy}{y+5}=\dfrac{dx}{x-3}\)

\(\Rightarrow 2\log|y+5|=\log|x-3|+C\)

\(\Rightarrow (y+5)^2=C_1(x-3)\)

\(\because\) the conic passes through \((4,-2)\),

\(9=C_1\)

\(\Rightarrow (y+5)^2=9(x-3)\)

Comparing with \((y-k)^2=4a(x-h)\), \(h=3,\ k=-5,\ 4a=9\)

\(\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{9}{4}\)

The focus is \(\left(3+\dfrac{9}{4},-5\right)=\left(\dfrac{21}{4},-5\right)\)

The focal distance of \((7,1)\) is \(d=\sqrt{\left(7-\dfrac{21}{4}\right)^2+(1+5)^2}\)

\(\Rightarrow d=\sqrt{\dfrac{49}{16}+36}\)

\(\Rightarrow d=\sqrt{\dfrac{625}{16}}=\dfrac{25}{4}\)

\(\Rightarrow 12d=75\)

The required value is \(75\).

questions.question:
Let L1,L2 be the lines passing through the point P(0,1) and touching the parabola 9x2+12x+18y-14=0. Let \(Q\) and \(R\) be the points on the lines L1 and L2 such that the ∆PQR is an isosceles triangle with base QR. If the slopes of the lines QR are m1 and m2, then 16m12+m22 is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let a line through \(P(0,1)\) have slope \(m\).

Its equation is \(y=mx+1\).

Substituting in \(9x^2+12x+18y-14=0\), we get \(9x^2+(12+18m)x+4=0\).

For tangency, \((12+18m)^2-4(9)(4)=0\).

\(\Rightarrow (12+18m)^2=144\)

\(\Rightarrow 12+18m=\pm12\)

\(\Rightarrow m=0,-\dfrac43\)

Unit direction vectors along the two tangents may be taken as \(\mathbf u_1=(1,0)\) and \(\mathbf u_2=\left(\dfrac35,-\dfrac45\right)\).

\(\because \triangle PQR\) is isosceles with base \(QR\), \(PQ=PR\).

For equal directed distances on the two lines, \(QR\) is parallel to \(\mathbf u_2-\mathbf u_1=\left(-\dfrac25,-\dfrac45\right)\), so one slope is \(m_1=2\).

For opposite directed distances, \(QR\) is parallel to \(-\mathbf u_2-\mathbf u_1=\left(-\dfrac85,\dfrac45\right)\), so the other slope is \(m_2=-\dfrac12\).

\(\therefore 16(m_1^2+m_2^2)=16\left(4+\dfrac14\right)=68\)

questions.question:
Let \(\vec{a}=2 \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}, \vec{b}=3 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}-5 \hat{k}\) and a vector \(\vec{c}\) be such that \(\vec{a} \times(\vec{b}+\vec{c})+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}=\hat{i}+8 \hat{j}+13 \hat{k}\). If \(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}=13\), then \((24-\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})\) is equal to.......

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(\vec c=x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k\).

\(\vec a\times(\vec b+\vec c)+\vec b\times\vec c=(y+z-1)\hat i+(-x-5z+22)\hat j+(-x+5y+17)\hat k\)

Comparing the components with \(\hat i+8\hat j+13\hat k\), we get

\(y+z-1=1\)

\(\Rightarrow y+z=2\)

\(-x-5z+22=8\)

\(\Rightarrow x+5z=14\)

\(-x+5y+17=13\)

\(\Rightarrow x-5y=4\)

Also, \(\vec a\cdot\vec c=13\).

\(2x-3y+4z=13\)

From \(y+z=2\), \(y=2-z\), and from \(x+5z=14\), \(x=14-5z\).

Substituting in \(2x-3y+4z=13\), we get

\(2(14-5z)-3(2-z)+4z=13\)

\(\Rightarrow 22-3z=13\)

\(\Rightarrow z=3\)

\(\Rightarrow y=-1\) and \(x=-1\)

\(\Rightarrow \vec b\cdot\vec c=3(-1)+4(-1)-5(3)=-22\)

\(\Rightarrow 24-\vec b\cdot\vec c=24-(-22)=46\)

The required value is \(46\).

questions.question:
Let P be the point (10,-2,-1) and Q be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point R(1,7,6) on the line passing through the points (2,-5,11) and (-6,7,-5). Then the length of the line segment \(PQ\) is equal to _____

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The line through \((2,-5,11)\) and \((-6,7,-5)\) has direction vector

\((-8,12,-16)=4(-2,3,-4)\)

Take \(A=(2,-5,11)\) and \(\vec d=(-2,3,-4)\).

Let \(R=(1,7,6)\) and let \(Q=A+t\vec d\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(R\).

\(\because RQ\perp\vec d\), \((R-Q)\cdot\vec d=0\)

\(\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{(R-A)\cdot\vec d}{|\vec d|^2}\)

\(\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{(-1,12,-5)\cdot(-2,3,-4)}{4+9+16}\)

\(\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{58}{29}=2\)

\(\Rightarrow Q=(2,-5,11)+2(-2,3,-4)=(-2,1,3)\)

For \(P=(10,-2,-1)\),

\(PQ=\sqrt{(-2-10)^2+(1+2)^2+(3+1)^2}\)

\(\Rightarrow PQ=\sqrt{144+9+16}=13\)

The required value is \(13\).
